headline: HBO Max and Paramount Plus to merge into a single streamer under Skydance
summary: Skydance's $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery will see the two streaming services unify over time, aiming to compete with Netflix.
details: Skydance has officially closed its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, a move that will lead to the eventual merger of HBO Max and Paramount Plus into a single streaming service.

The combined entity, operating under the Skydance umbrella, announced that both streamers will "unify into a single service over time." This strategic consolidation aims to bolster its subscriber base and competitive standing in the streaming market.

Skydance CEO David Ellison previously indicated that the merged service could command "a little over 200 million direct-to-consumer subscribers." However, specific details regarding the timeline for this integration and the final name of the unified platform remain undisclosed.

HBO CEO Casey Bloys is slated to oversee the merged streaming service. The consolidation is seen as a direct response to the dominance of platforms like Netflix, which reported 325 million subscribers in January.

This merger promises to bring together popular content from both services, including acclaimed titles such as "Mobland," "Yellowstone," "The White Lotus," and "House of the Dragon," onto one platform for consumers.

headline: Mistral AI unveils Mistral Large 4 with 1T parameters, challenging rivals
summary: Mistral AI's new ML4 model, nicknamed 'Le Chonk', boasts 1 trillion parameters and aims to compete with both open and closed AI models. Its weights will be released in three weeks after safety testing.
details: French AI lab Mistral AI has released Mistral Large 4 (ML4), a new large multimodal model designed to compete with leading AI models from both American and Chinese companies. The model, nicknamed 'Le Chonk' due to its 1 trillion parameters, is positioned as an alternative to the growing divide between closed and open-weight AI.

While ML4 is not yet an open-weight model, Mistral plans to make its weights publicly available in three weeks following comprehensive safety testing. This phased release aims to ensure the model's weights can be used for defense rather than malicious attacks, addressing mounting security concerns.

Mistral emphasizes that ML4 was trained entirely on its own compute infrastructure, utilizing approximately 4,000 Nvidia GPUs. This is reportedly two to three times less than its Chinese competitors and significantly less than what closed-source competitors use, highlighting Mistral's efficient training methods.

Although benchmark results are still pending, Mistral anticipates ML4 will be a top performer among open-weight models. The company also believes it could outperform closed models in specific customer-critical areas, particularly where its multimodal capabilities can add significant value.

ML4 is optimized for use cases such as cybersecurity and finance, and notably, chip design. This focus aligns with Mistral's key backers, including ASML and Samsung, who are major players in the semiconductor industry.

Mistral emphasizes that ML4 was trained entirely on its own compute infrastructure, utilizing approximately 4,000 Nvidia GPUs. This is reportedly two to three times less than its Chinese competitors and significantly less than what closed-source competitors use, highlighting Mistral's efficient training methods.

Although benchmark results are still pending, Mistral anticipates ML4 will be a top performer among open-weight models. The company also believes it could outperform closed models in specific customer-critical areas, particularly where its multimodal capabilities can add significant value.

ML4 is optimized for use cases such as cybersecurity and finance, and notably, chip design. This focus aligns with Mistral's key backers, including ASML and Samsung, who are major players in the semiconductor industry.
